about: R036 (1), T5 (dossier §18.161 (3)): the reviewed termination arguments for every tailRec-family use, JS loop and reference cycle that test/readback-total-scan.mjs finds in the src module closure of Features.Check.Strategy.ReadBack.Package. Evidence for review, not a proof of totality or exception freedom; docs/plans/2026-11-04-readback-termination-audit.md. A new loop or cycle fails test/structure-readback-total.test.mjs until it has a row here.

entries.argument: Derived Traversable on Arithmetic: the dictionary refers to itself because its sequence is traverse(traversableArithmetic) with identity. Arithmetic is not recursive (Binary holds an operator and two operands of the parameter type), so traverse applies the supplied function once to each operand and combines the results with the Binary constructor through map and apply (the supplied Applicative decides whether and how often that constructor runs); traverse contains no recursive call, neither to itself nor to sequence. The cycle is one step (sequence to traverse) and does not recur.
Derived Eq on TypeName (no arrow constructor): structural recursion on strict subterms (arguments, labels) of two finite values.
Self tail call compiled to a loop ($tco): each step goes from an Arrow to its rest, a strict subterm of both finite spines; it stops at the first non-arrow or mismatch.
The compiled loop body of sameSpine's self tail call (the loop row above): it is called once per iteration of that loop, not recursively.

Hand-written Eq: eq is sameSpine, which walks two arrows' spines by its compiled $tco loop (the loop row) and recurses with `==` only into parameters, records' fields and applications' arguments, strict subterms of two finite values.
Derived Eq on MTy: structural recursion on strict subterms of two finite values, MArrow spines included (one frame per arrow; no loop), so as deep as the spine.
Counting loop over a written type's FunRef spine: each step moves to the FunRef's result, a strict subterm; the second pass (mapAccumL) takes exactly the counted steps.
Spine loop over two arrows in step: each step moves both to their results (strict subterms); it stops when either is not an arrow or a stage differs.
Spine loop over two arrows in step: each step moves both to their results (strict subterms); it stops when either is not an arrow or a stage orders them.

Spine loop through `look`: each step moves to the arrow's result. With `look` = identity (substitute, traverseTy) that is a strict subterm. With a substitution's walk (Subst.resolve) it ends if the substitution is acyclic, which `unify`'s occurs check maintains (reasoned; the read-back's closure calls it with identity only).
Hand-written Eq on Ty: arrows compared by Compare.sameSpines's loop; recursion only into data arguments, rows, handler labels and records, strict subterms of two finite values.
Hand-written Ord on Ty: arrows ordered by Compare.compareSpines's loop; recursion only into data arguments, rows, handler parts and records, strict subterms of two finite values.

Counts up from `fresh` while the made row variable is in `taken`, a finite map: at most |taken| + 1 steps.

Robinson unification in Martelli and Montanari's form (JACM 1982), with Rémy's row rule, over a triangular θ (Triangular: an equation is read through θ when taken). Each step removes an equation, replaces one by equations on strict subterms of the equation read under θ, or binds a flexible variable (occurs-checked against the image read under θ, so θ stays acyclic) that later equations then read through θ; R5's two-tail case binds two variables and makes one fresh. Measure, taken on equations read under θ: (unbound flexible variables, total equation size), lexicographic. Reasoned, not machine-checked; the read-back's closure reaches it only through the type read-back's θ.
Layered search: each layer adds to `seen` only bound variables not yet in it, from θ's finite domain; a layer that adds none leaves an empty frontier, which ends the loop. At most |dom θ| + 1 layers.

Local helpers of one layer (`visit` folds over the finite frontier; `inserted` and `found` name values): the cycle is a naming artifact of where-bindings referring to each other, with no recursive call.

Follows a meta's binding chain in the store. It ends because the bindings are acyclic: UnifyMark binds only a chain's unbound end meta, to the other chain's end, when the two ends differ (reasoned from UnifyMark `equateMarks`; not checked here). The read-back reads the store through Least, not through this loop.

Union-find root search (Galler and Fischer 1964): `union` links one root to a different root only, so parent links form a forest and the chain from a node to its root is finite (at most one step per node). Fuelled copy with an agreement check: test/r0-readback-least-fuel.test.mjs.

Kleene iteration of a monotone map (insertWith Set.union only adds a root's entry or grows it) on a finite lattice: maps from the finitely many roots to sets of the finitely many constants, an absent root below the empty set, of height roots × (constants + 1); so a fixpoint within roots × (constants + 1) + 1 passes (Davey and Priestley, Introduction to Lattices and Order, ch. 8). Fuelled copy with an agreement check: test/r0-readback-least-fuel.test.mjs.
